elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 states that Customer commits to purchase “no minimum amount,” and § 12.3 confirms that Customer has made no “minimum-volume” commitment.

elements.element: Customer pays only for Services ordered or used.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly provides that Customer “pays only for Services ordered or used,” eliminating payment for an unmet minimum.

elements.element: If any commitment applies, it is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: No commitment applies: § 2.1 sets the minimum at zero and § 12.3 disclaims any minimum-volume commitment. The condition for this duration restriction is therefore demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If any commitment applies, Customer may reduce it on 30 days’ notice.
elements.evidence: No commitment applies, so there is nothing requiring a reduction right. The condition for this requirement is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If Customer has a commitment shortfall, it is resolved through a true-up.
elements.evidence: Because there is no minimum commitment, Customer cannot incur a commitment shortfall requiring a true-up.

elements.element: No penalty applies for a commitment shortfall.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 removes the take-or-pay obligation and limits payment to Services ordered or used, leaving no penalty for an unmet commitment.

result.reason: The operative language fully reaches the preferred position by eliminating the minimum and take-or-pay obligation and limiting payment to ordered or used Services. It consequently also satisfies the conditional fallback protections because no commitment or shortfall can arise. The change is targeted and consistent with § 12.3. Drafting quality is slightly reduced by the awkward, unnecessary phrase “commits to purchase no minimum amount ... in each of the next three years,” though § 12.3 removes material ambiguity.
